ai_show_review.summary: Seething Dancin' In The Street set with soaring Morning Dew
ai_show_review.blurb: The MIT free concert erupts with a blistering 'Dancin' In The Street' and a soaring 'Morning Dew'. Jerry's guitar shreds while Phil lays down devastating bass runs, and Pigpen fuels the groove on 'Good Lovin''. Tight transitions keep the energy high throughout the set.
ai_show_review.review:
On May 6 1970 the Grateful Dead turned Kresge Plaza into a political rally‑turned‑rock‑show. From the opening burst of "Dancin' In The Street"—where Garcia’s SG was described as “thrashing” and “ripping like a monster”—the band never let up, feeding the crowd’s outrage with raw intensity. Pigpen’s organ and harmonica added gritty color on the double‑take of "Good Lovin'", while Phil Lesh delivered one of his most devastating bass runs, especially in the climactic moments of both "Dancin'" and "Morning Dew". The seamless segue into the classic "China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider" kept the momentum rolling into a soulful "Next Time You See Me" before soaring again on the hauntingly beautiful "Morning Dew". A second‑half surge through "Saint Stephen" (with its fiery transition into "Not Fade Away") and the double‑drummed groove of Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart cemented this set as a tightly focused, high‑energy statement that still feels fresh today.

Across all available soundboard sources the performance shines: the Gans Hall SBD (gd1970-05-06.sbd.gans-hall.95.shnf) offers crystal‑clear balance despite a few vintage mic quirks, while the other SBD captures reinforce the same ferocious playing and tight set flow. Even the enthusiastic audience tape captures Jerry’s dynamic range—from thunderous attack to nuanced nuance—proving that this historic free concert is as compelling on the floor as it is in the archives.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All five recordings are marked positive; reviewers repeatedly praise the set’s intensity, Jerry’s ferocious guitar work, Phil’s bass leads, and Pigpen’s organ on Good Lovin'. Consistent high‑energy descriptions across sources justify a strong positive adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Provides a clear, well‑balanced soundboard mix that captures the raw intensity and tight set flow with only minor vintage distortion.

key_highlights: Incendiary "Dancin' In The Street" opening that sets a political, high‑octane tone.
"Morning Dew" soars with emotive vocals and Phil’s prominent bass.
Powerful double‑take of "Good Lovin'" showcasing Jerry’s long solo and Pigpen’s organ/harmonica grit.
Tight segues, especially the classic "China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider" and the fiery transition from "Saint Stephen" into "Not Fade Away".

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a self‑generating source of electricity, ripping through "Dancin'" and laying down an extended, ferocious solo on "Good Lovin'", while his tone is praised as alive, intense, and monster‑like throughout.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides devastating bass runs, especially in the climax of "Dancin'" and the soaring moments of "Morning Dew", driving the improvisation with a lead‑bass approach that fuels the band’s fire.
band_performance.Bob: Weir shares vocal duties on "Dancin' In The Street" and supports rhythmically; his vocals are noted around the split‑off announcement after "Not Fade Away".
band_performance.Keys: Pigpen’s organ and harmonica add vital grit on "Good Lovin'", with quirky mic moments that give character, while also contributing supportive keys during the mellow middle of "Dancin'."
band_performance.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (and Mickey Hart) create a dynamic soundscape; strong intro on "Good Lovin'" and steady grooves keep the tempo warm as the band warms their hands.
